## SECTION 0 — ANALYSIS OVERVIEW

- **Security**: Digi International Inc. (Nasdaq: DGII), Communication Equipment / Industrial IoT
- **T0 (analysis date)**: 2026-09-07. Price $69.36 [Aggregator – vendor quote]. Shares outstanding 37.94M; diluted ~39.1M [Actual – Q4 FY26 guidance assumption]
- **Market cap**: $2.632B [Arithmetic on vendor price and share count]
- **Enterprise value**: ~$2.71B at T0 ($2.632B equity + $81M net debt per management Q3 FY26, + ~$12M operating leases [Actual – call transcript 2026-08-05 and Section 6B])
- **T-1 financial reference**: Q3 FY26 (quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-08-05): revenue $138.7M, GAAP operating margin 16.5%, ARR $191M, adjusted EBITDA $40.4M [Actual – Motley Fool transcript of the Q3 FY26 call]
- **Tpf events**: FY26 guidance raised to revenue $529–533M, adjusted EBITDA $146–147.5M; management re-affirmed FY2028 targets of $200M adjusted EBITDA (and $200M ARR, which the data show to be effectively already reached or superseded) [Actual – company call, 2026-08-05]
- **Website verification**: Pack data were checked against the live Q1 FY26 press release, the Q3 FY26 earnings call, and the company's acquisition announcements; pack actuals reconcile (FY25 revenue $430M = four quarters ending Sep-2025; 9M FY26 GAAP net income $39M matches the quarterly rows).
- **Model type**: Product–Platform Hybrid (Archetype D) → **Engine 3** (Hybrid Core + Platform/ARR valuation), cross-checked with a 10-year semi-transparent DCF and EV/adjusted EBITDA against the company's FY2028 targets.
- **Result**: Expected intrinsic value ≈ **$75/share** (probability-weighted across scenarios); base case ≈ **$76**. Margin of safety at T0 ≈ **+7.5%** — **inadequate** for a new full position. **Verdict: HOLD / no new money at $69.36; actionable buy zone $58–62.**

## SECTION 1.5 — BASE RATE & HISTORICAL PATTERN

**Step 1.5-1 — Standard reference base rates for relevant classifiers**

| Classifier | Standard base rate | This company |
|---|---|---|
| Mature industrial-tech hardware/software platform "successful" 5-year survival | ~75–85% | Met (40+ years operating; FY25 OCF $108M positive) |
| Platform transition to >30% recurring revenue | **~20–30%** [Reference] | **Met and exceeded**: ARR/revenue = 36%; ARR $191M at Q3 FY26 (+52% YoY) [Actual – call] |
| Sustained double-digit organic revenue growth 5+ years post-transition | ~30–40% | Not yet proven; FY26 ~+23.5% [Actual] but >1/3 of increment is Jolt + Particle |

| Serial small-cap M&A (tuck-ins) additive to ROIC | ~40–50% at 2–4x EBITDA; lower at 10x+ if integration fails | Jolt at ~$145.5M / ~$10–12M EBITDA ≈ 12–15x [Estimate] |

**Step 1.5-2 — Deviation from base rate**

The bull case for this name assumes a successful platform transition — which the market has re-rated in the last 12 months (+126.6% 52-week return [Actual – Yahoo]). Reason to accept deviation from the ~25% platform-transition success base rate:
1. ARR already **$191M** and growing 52% [Actual] — if this were a failed transition, ARR would not have reached 36% of revenue;
2. GAAP operating margin has expanded from mid-single-digit (12-yr median 5.1% [Arithmetic on pack]) to 16.5% [Actual] — economics confirm the model, not just the narrative;
3. Management has a defined acquisition playbook with FY2026 EBITDA guidance raised twice in 2 quarters; balance-sheet deleveraging is on plan (net debt $104M Dec-25 → $81M at Jun-26, −$23M in one quarter [Actual]).

**Step 1.5-3 — Base-rate shock check: PASS.** The bull case does not exceed 1.5x the platform-transition base rate; no re-evaluation triggered.

## SECTION 2 — BUSINESS QUALITY

**Step 2-1 — Business understanding**
Digi designs and sells mission-critical IoT hardware (routers, gateways, console servers under the Digi, Opengear, and legacy brands) into equipment that spans healthcare, retail, industrial automation, data centers/edge. It monetizes the installed base through software/services: Digi Remote Manager, extended warranties, technical support, cellular connectivity (Ventus), and wireless sensing/monitoring (SmartSense). It adds field-service and developer-cloud platforms through acquisitions (Jolt in Aug-2025; Particle announced Jan-2026), growing recurring revenue.
**Understandability: High.** Product → recurring-software attach is a textbook hybrid model; no financial engineering complexity.

**Step 2-2 — Moat assessment + direction**

| Moat type | Score (0–3) | Direction |
|---|---|---|
| Intangible assets | 2 | Stable — 40-yr brand, proprietary firmware |
| Switching costs | 3 | **Widening** — embedded devices with 10–15 yr lifecycles; SmartSense compliance data across locations |
| Network effects | 1 | Stable — Particle ecosystem is the only true network asset; early |
| Cost advantage | 1 | Stable — asset-light, but no structural cost edge |
| Economies of scale | 2 | Widening — R&D leverage on $530M+ revenue |
| Regulatory barriers | 1 | Stable — FDA/healthcare/utility certifications create barriers but not exclusive |
| Data moat | 1 | Widening — operational data assets from SmartSense/Ventus/Jolt |
| **Total** | **11/21** | **Widening** |

Verdict: **Narrow moat, widening** (11 = narrow-to-wide boundary). Not a fortress.

**Step 2-3 — Lynch classification**
**Hybrid: Fast Grower + Cyclical.** The recurring/ARR side (36% and rising) is a fast grower; the one-time hardware side (≈64%) is cyclical (data-center and industrial capex). Lynch framework says you pay for one story; the market is currently paying for both.

**Step 2-4 — Financial strength scorecard** [all consistent with pack + Q3 FY26 call]

- Revenue growth: FY25 $430M; FY26E $529–533M (+23.5% guide) [Actual]; TTM $506M [Actual]
- Gross margin: FY25 63.0%; Q3 FY26 64.8%, +130bps [Actual]
- Adjusted EBITDA: FY25 ~$108M; FY26E $146–147.5M (+35–36%) [Actual — call]
- GAAP operating margin: 16.5% (Q3 FY26) [Actual]
- GAAP net income: FY25 $41M; TTM $49M [Actual]
- OCF: FY25 $108M; Q3 FY26 QTD $33M (+38% YoY) [Actual]
- Balance sheet: net debt $81M = ~0.55x FY26E adjusted EBITDA [Actual + arithmetic]
- Working capital: current ratio 1.2x (Sep-25: current assets $131M / current liabilities $108M per pack) — adequate, not strong
- **Verdict: Good.**

**Step 2-5 — Capital allocation scorecard**
1. **Buyback efficiency: 1/3** — no meaningful buyback; 2-3% SBC-driven dilution/year (share count +2.0% in FY25 [Actual])
2. **M&A track record: 3/3** — SmartSense, Opengear, Jolt, Particle; OCF > adjusted EBITDA shows acquisitions are cash-accretive at the company level; Jolt/Particle revenue already inside FY26 guidance (three raises in two quarters) [Actual]
3. **Capex efficiency: 2/3** — very low capex ($3M FY25) is appropriate for the model; ROIC not yet proven > WACC + 3% with goodwill included
4. **Mix rationality: 2/3** — clear "acquire → integrate → generate → compound" strategy internally consistent; but the $145.5M Jolt price was ~12–15x EBITDA, not a distressed price; Particle's initial EBITDA contribution is only $1–2M vs ~$50M+ purchase price [Estimate]
5. **Guidance accuracy: 3/3** — FY26 revenue/EBITDA raised twice; met or beat in the data-available quarters
- **Insider ownership bonus**: no cluster-buy data retrieved [Unconfirmed]
- **Total = 11/15** — good.

## SECTION 2.5 — INTANGIBLES-ADJUSTED FINANCIALS

**Step 2.5-1 — R&D capitalization**: FY26E R&D ≈ $75M [Assumption based on Q3 FY26 R&D of $20.3M [Actual]]. Capitalizing at 4-yr amortization adds ~$15M to adjusted operating income (R&D expense $75M − amortization of previously capitalized R&D ≈ $60M deferred increase). Implication: true pre-tax return on tangible capital is higher than GAAP suggests because the business is generating a *reinvested-invisible-asset* surplus.

**Step 2.5-2 — SBC treatment**: SBC — FY25 $15M (3.5% of revenue) [Actual — pack]. Owner FCF must deduct it. FY26E SBC ≈ $20M [Assumption: revenue × 3.8%].

**Step 2.5-3 — Lease capitalization**: immaterial — balance sheet already carries $12M operating lease ROU asset [Actual — pack 6B].

**Step 2.5-4 — Brand / data assets**: SmartSense compliance data, Opengear's remote network tooling, Particle's developer base (≈$20–22M ARR acquired [Actual — Q1 FY26 digest]) — not capitalized in this analysis beyond their cash flows.

**Step 2.5-5 — Adjusted ROIC**:
- GAAP net operating profit after tax (FY25): ~$31M (NI $41M − excess tax on D&A); after adjusting for R&D capitalization and acquisition amortization: ~$45M [Estimate].
- Invested capital including goodwill/intangibles: ~$650M (equity $636M + debt $159M − cash $22M) [Actual — pack].
- **Adjusted ROIC ≈ 7–9%**; return on *tangible* invested capital (excluding ~$450M goodwill/intangibles [Estimate]) ≈ **14–16%**.
- Gap explanation: goodwill from acquisitions is the difference. This is the crux of the investment: whether Jolt/Particle earn their purchase price.

**Step 2.5-6 — Owner earnings (Buffett)**: Owner FCF = OCF − SBC − maintenance capex:
- FY25: $108M − $15M − ~$2M ≈ **$91M** [Actual]
- FY26E: ≈ $147M − $20M − ~$5M ≈ **$122M** [Assumption + Actual]

## SECTION 3 — VALUATION (ENGINE 3: PRODUCT–PLATFORM HYBRID)

**Step 3-1 — Segment structure (FY26E estimate)**
- **Product segment (Consisting of devices + software attach)**: FY26E revenue ≈ $380M (Q1 $86M; Q2 ~$94M; Q3 $100M; Q4E ~$101M [Arithmetic on pack + guidance]); ARR ≈ $75–80M by FY26-end (incl. Particle) [Estimate]
- **Solutions segment (SmartSense, Ventus, Jolt)**: FY26E revenue ≈ $151M (Q1 $36M; Q2 ~$37M; Q3 $39M; Q4E ~$39M); ARR ≈ $131M at Q3-end [Actual + arithmetic]
- **Blended**: ARR ≈ $200M at FY26-end; revenue ≈ $531M; ARR/revenue ≈ 38% [Estimate]

**Step 3-2 — Hybrid cross-check via implied multiples**

- T0 EV/FY26E adjusted EBITDA = $2,710M / $147M = **18.4x** [Arithmetic]
- T0 EV/FY26E revenue = **5.1x**
- Cost-of-equity fair value (below) implies a **fair EV/adjusted EBITDA of ≈ 19.8x** on 2026E — i.e., the market is paying roughly the correct multiple *if and only if* the company hits its 2028 EBITDA target.

**Step 3-3 — Explicit DCF (base case)**

**Discount-rate derivation**:
- Risk-free rate: 4.5% (long-term normalized, anchored on 4.85% current 10-yr) [Assumption + Actual]
- ERP: 4.8% [Assumption]
- Beta: 1.00 (listed 0.97 [Aggregator]; we round to 1.0 for the 26% earnings beta of a small-cap hybrid) [Assumption]
- Cost of equity: 4.5% + 1.0 × 4.8% = **9.3%** (blend with 9.6% if using current 10-yr → use **9.5%**)
- After-tax cost of debt: ~5.5% [Estimate]
- Weights: E = 97%, D = 3% (net debt/EV = 3%) → **WACC ≈ 9.4%**; for conservatism, use **9.6%** as cost of equity to equity-FCF and a haircut for cash-flow risk.

**Explicit forecast (all $M) — Base case**

| FY | Revenue | Growth | Adj. EBITDA | Margin | SBC | Capex | OCF (= EBITDA) | FCFE (OCF − SBC − Capex) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026E | $531 | +23.5% [Actual guide] | $147 | 27.7% [Actual guide] | $20 | $5 | $147 | **$122** |
| 2027E | $590 | +11% [Assumption: 9–10% organic + bolt-on rollover] | $173 | 29.3% [Assumption: mgmt. path to 2028] | $22 | $6 | $173 | **$145** |
| 2028E | $655 | +11% [Assumption: aligns to $200M EBITDA target] | $200 | 30.5% [Assumption: mgmt. target] | $25 | $7 | $200 | **$168** |
| 2029E | $720 | +10% [Assumption] | $226 | 31.4% | $27 | $8 | $226 | **$191** |
| 2030E | $790 | +10% [Assumption] | $252 | 31.9% | $30 | $9 | $252 | **$213** |
| Terminal | — | +3.5% [Assumption — ≤ nominal GDP 4%] | — | — | — | — | — | TV = $3,614 undiscounted |

D&A is excluded from the FCFE definition because OCF conversion empirically equals adjusted EBITDA (FY25: OCF = adj EBITDA ≈ $108M [Actual]; FY26 YTD confirms ~1.0x). SBC is fully deducted from owner FCF — this is the pack's data-discipline instruction applied.

**FCF to equity discounting @ 9.6% — present values**
- FY26E (Year 1) PV = $122 / 1.096 = **$111M**
- FY27E = $145 / 1.201 = **$121M**
- FY28E = $168 / 1.317 = **$128M**
- FY29E = $191 / 1.443 = **$132M**
- FY30E = $213 / 1.582 = **$135M**
- Terminal value = $213 × 1.035 / (0.096 − 0.035) = **$3,614M**; PV = **$2,284M**
- Implied total equity value ≈ **$2,911M** ≈ **$75.6 per share** (at ~38.5M diluted shares)

**Tornado sensitivity (TPG at $75.6)**

| Variable | −1σ | Base | +1σ | Valuation range |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY28E adj. EBITDA | $170M | $200M | $230M | $64–87 |
| Discount rate | 8.6% | 9.6% | 10.6% | $85–68 |
| Terminal growth | 2.5% | 3.5% | 4.5% | $68–85 |

Top 3 value-driver KPIs: **(1)** FY28 adjusted EBITDA ≥ $200M; **(2)** OCF conversion ≥ 1.0× adj. EBITDA; **(3)** cost of equity ≤ 10% (i.e., the Fed does not force a small-cap multiple reset).

Competitive countermove impact: −1 (recurring, but not existential).

**Step 3.5-3 — Customer lifecycle**: Early-adopter demand in AI/data-center edge is running 25%+ growth; mainstream industrial adoption is mid-cycle. LTV/CAC headwinds are possible as the easy conversions finish.

## SECTION 6.5 — KELLY SIZING

Using the 25/50/25 probability distribution:
- Expected arithmetic return ≈ 0.25(−30%) + 0.50(+9%) + 0.25(+44%) = **+8.0%**
- Variance ≈ 685 → σ ≈ 26.2%
- **Full Kelly ≈ 1.2% of capital; half-Kelly ≈ 0.6%**
Given estimation risk and macro headwind, use **quarter-Kelly ≈ 0.5% initial**; scale toward 2% only on margin-of-safety confirmation. The gap between conviction sizing (4–6%) and Kelly sizing (~0.6%) is >20pct and triggers Rule 13 — resolves in favor of the *smaller* Kelly size because valuation headroom is thin.

- The portfolio hedge is to keep size small and use limit entries; no delta-1 index hedge is advised for a 0.5–2% position.

## SECTION 8 — MONITORING RULES (THESIS KPIs)

Quarterly triggers that invalidate/confirm the thesis:
1. **ARR**: ≥ 27% growth in FY26; ≥ 22% in FY27. Below 15% → thesis broken.
2. **Adjusted EBITDA margin**: 27.5% FY26 → 29% FY27 → 30.5% FY28.
3. **OCF conversion**: OCF / adjusted EBITDA ≥ 0.95 each quarter.
4. **Net leverage**: below 1.0x EBITDA sustained; debt pay-down in Q4 FY26 ≥ $20M [Assumption].
5. **Integration**: Jolt + Particle churn < 2%/quarterand organic ARR, ex-acquisitions, > 20%.
6. Share dilution: diluted share count above 40.5M by FY28 → thesis fails.
7. **Red-line**: inventory > $60M or receivables DSO > 60 days signals channel-stuffing risk.

**Step 7-4 — Pre-mortem** ("If this fails by 2030, why?")
1. **Multiple crash precedes the fundamentals**: late-2026 Fed hike crushes growth-stock multiples; DGII falls 40% despite operational execution. Early warning: 10-year > 5.2% + valuation > 20x forward EBITDA.
2. **The acquisitions were value-destructive**: Particle/Jolt fail to cross-sell; ARR growth stays high but EBITDA conversion fails because of transition costs. Warning: ARR grows 25% while EBITDA margin stalls below 28%.
3. **AI-era competitive death by bundling**: Cisco/Verizon bundle console + monitoring; Opengear loses a key neo-cloud account. Warning: quarterly opengear revenue −20% YoY.

**Step 7-5 — Decision journal**: T0 price $69.36. Base fair value $75.6. Bear $48.6. Bull $100.0. Est. expected value $75.0. Key assumptions: FY28E EBITDA $200M; 9.6% cost of equity; OCF=adj EBITDA. Red-team concerns: FY28 target is a *company-sourced* estimate, not an independent verification; acquisition execution is unproven at this scale.

## SECTION 9 — RED TEAM (ADVERSARIAL)

**9-1 — Short thesis (5–7 bullets):**
- $69.36 = **18.4x forward adjusted EBITDA** (and 55x GAAP EPS); priced for perfect execution with zero MoS.
- More than 1/3 of FY26's stated +23.5% growth comes from **Jolt + Particle, not organic**; organic growth is ~12-15%, not the 25% story.
- The "adjusted EBITDA" target excludes SBC, acquisition amortization, and integration costs — real owner earnings are ~20% below management-adjusted figures.
